t: Advanced Appointment Booking & Scheduling < 2.7 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary User Registration
d: The Advanced Appointment Booking & Scheduling WordPress plugin before 2.7 does not verify the site's user-registration setting before creating accounts through a publicly accessible shortcode, allowing unauthenticated attackers to register arbitrary user accounts, and be automatically logged in, even when user registration is disabled on the site.

t: WP Duplicate <= 1.1.11 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload via Authentication Bypass
d: The WP Duplicate WordPress plugin through 1.1.11 does not properly verify a request authentication value and does not validate the path or type of uploaded files, making it possible for unauthenticated attackers to write arbitrary files to the server and achieve remote code execution. This vulnerability is being actively exploited in the wild.

t: WooCommerce Stripe Payment Gateway 10.9.0 - 11.0.1 - Customer Password Stored in Plaintext via Express Checkout
d: The WooCommerce Stripe Payment Gateway WordPress plugin before 11.1.0 does not exclude the account password from the checkout fields it saves to order metadata during express checkout, causing the password a customer chooses when creating an account at checkout to be stored in plaintext in the database, readable by anyone with access to order data or the database. Version 10.9.0 stored the passwords. Version 10.9.1 stopped new ones from being stored but left existing ones in place, and version 11.1.0 removes them on update. Passwords stored this way should be considered exposed.

t: GemBooking < 1.7.1 - Staff+ Arbitrary Post Deletion and Site Settings Update via REST Context Check Bypass
d: The GemBooking WordPress plugin before 1.7.1 does not properly verify that a REST request is addressed to its own routes before temporarily granting staff users administrative capabilities, allowing users with the GemBooking WordPress plugin before 1.7.1's Staff role to delete arbitrary posts and update the site's settings.

t: Event Tickets Manager for WooCommerce 1.5.4 - 1.5.9 - Unauthenticated Site-wide Event Ticket Price Manipulation
d: The Event Tickets Manager for WooCommerce WordPress plugin before 1.6.0 does not validate the ticket-type price sent to one of its unauthenticated AJAX actions when the referenced product has no ticket types configured, and stores the submitted price site-wide, where it is applied to the next event ticket added to any cart, allowing unauthenticated visitors to buy event tickets at an arbitrary price, including for free. This is due to an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-34898.

t: GemBooking < 1.7.1 - Unauthenticated Team Member Double-Booking via Cross-Object Race Condition
d: The GemBooking WordPress plugin before 1.7.1 does not serialise concurrent booking requests per team member, allowing unauthenticated users to create overlapping confirmed bookings for the same team member across different bookable items by sending simultaneous requests.

t: Vigilant < 2.11.0 - 2FA Bypass via Third-Party Login Forms
d: The Vigilant WordPress plugin before 2.11.0 does not enforce its two-factor authentication on login forms other than the default WordPress one, allowing an attacker who knows a user's password to skip the second factor and log in as that user.

t: UniPAY Payment Gateway For WooCommerce < 2.4 - Unauthenticated Order Key and Customer PII Disclosure
d: The UniPAY Payment Gateway For WooCommerce WordPress plugin before 2.4 does not perform any authorization check before returning an order's order-received URL for an attacker-supplied order id, exposing the order's secret key in the redirect and allowing unauthenticated attackers to enumerate orders and disclose customers' personal data (name, email address, phone number and address).

t: WP BASE Booking of Appointments, Services and Events 6.5.0 - Subscriber+ Privilege Escalation
d: The WP BASE Booking of Appointments, Services and Events WordPress plugin before 6.5.1 does not properly restrict access to one of its user-creation actions, allowing authenticated users with Subscriber-level access and above to create a new administrator account and thereby escalate their privileges.
r: WP BASE Booking of Appointments, Services and Events

t: Post Duplicator < 3.0.18 - Admin+ Privilege Escalation via Unvalidated Capability Assignment
d: The Post Duplicator WordPress plugin before 3.0.18 does not validate the capabilities assigned to roles through its permissions settings, allowing a site administrator on a multisite network who is not a Super Admin to grant any role arbitrary capabilities, including the network-management capabilities reserved to the Super Admin.

t: Post Duplicator < 3.0.18 - Admin+ Arbitrary Option Update via Unvalidated Option Name
d: The Post Duplicator WordPress plugin before 3.0.18 does not restrict settings saves to its own options, allowing a site administrator on a multisite network who is not a Super Admin to overwrite arbitrary options of their site, including the role definitions, and so grant themselves network-management capabilities.

t: Fusion Page Builder < 1.7.1 - Contributor+ Arbitrary Post Trashing via IDOR
d: The Fusion Page Builder WordPress plugin before 1.7.1 does not check that the user owns the content it moves to the trash, which could allow users with a role as low as Contributor to trash arbitrary posts and pages, or delete them permanently where the trash is disabled.

t: All-in-One Video Gallery < 5.1.1 - Unauthenticated Password-Protected Video Disclosure via Player Page and Download Handler
d: The All-in-One Video Gallery WordPress plugin before 5.1.1 does not check whether a video is password protected before serving it through its standalone player page and its download link, allowing unauthenticated visitors to obtain the media source of password-protected videos, such as unlisted YouTube or Vimeo links and external file URLs.

t: Limit Login Attempts Reloaded < 3.4.1 - Two-Factor Authentication Bypass via Malformed X-Forwarded-For Header
d: The Limit Login Attempts Security WordPress plugin before 3.4.1 does not confirm that its two-factor authentication step succeeded before completing a login and treats a failure to build that step as success, so an attacker who holds a protected user's password can bypass the second factor by sending a request header that breaks the step.

t: Limit Login Attempts Reloaded 3.0.0 - 3.4.0 - Two-Factor Authentication Bypass via XML-RPC
d: The Limit Login Attempts Security WordPress plugin before 3.4.1 does not enforce its two-factor authentication on every password-authentication route, so an attacker who already knows a protected user's password can authenticate through an alternative login interface and obtain that user's access without completing the second factor.

t: Mail Debug for WooCommerce <= 1.3.0 - Unauthenticated Sent Email Disclosure Leading to Account Takeover
d: The Mail Debug for WooCommerce WordPress plugin through 1.3.0 does not perform any capability, authentication, or nonce check on one of its email-logging actions, which is exposed to unauthenticated users and is not restricted to its own data, allowing anyone to read the full body of every email the site has sent, including password-reset emails whose reset key lets an attacker take over an administrator account.

t: Grand Job <= 1.2.1 - Unauthenticated Account Takeover via Empty Password Reset Code
d: The Grand Job WordPress plugin through 1.2.1 does not correctly verify the password reset code before updating a user's password, allowing unauthenticated attackers to set the password of arbitrary accounts, including administrators, and fully take over the site.

t: EASY-JS-WPAPI <= 2.0 - Unauthenticated Administrator Password Disclosure and Authentication Bypass
d: The EASY-JS-WPAPI Client HANDLE for the WordPress REST-API WordPress plugin through 2.0 does not prevent the administrator credentials it stores from being disclosed to unauthenticated users and does not correctly verify authentication, allowing unauthenticated attackers to obtain administrator credentials and gain full administrator access to the site.
r: EASY-JS-WPAPI Client HANDLE for the WordPress REST-API

t: mView <= 1.0.3 - Subscriber+ Arbitrary File Upload
d: The mView 豆瓣电影 WordPress plugin through 1.0.3 does not validate the type, name, or source of a remotely fetched file, nor perform any capability or authorization check, before saving it to a web-accessible directory, allowing any authenticated user such as a subscriber to upload arbitrary PHP files and achieve remote code execution.

t: AZEXO Store Locator <= 1.4 - Subscriber+ Arbitrary File Write via azt_items_import
d: The AZEXO Store Locator WordPress plugin through 1.4 does not perform capability or nonce checks on its AJAX actions and does not sanitise a request header used to build a file path, allowing any authenticated user such as a subscriber to write a file with an arbitrary name, location, and content, leading to remote code execution.

t: Open redirect in the Liberty ID-FF service provider single sign-on flow
d: OpenAM (OpenAM Consortium Edition) 14.0.5 and earlier contains an open redirect vulnerability (CWE-601) in the Liberty ID-FF service provider single sign-on flow. The goto parameter of the /preLogin endpoint is stored as the RelayState of the Liberty ID-FF authentication request without validation, and after the user completes single sign-on at the identity provider, the assertion consumer service redirects the browser to that value. A remote unauthenticated attacker can induce a user to access a crafted URL and, after the user authenticates, redirect the user to an arbitrary website, which may be used for phishing. Only deployments in which a Liberty ID-FF hosted service provider is configured are affected; Liberty ID-FF is not configured by default. This issue is fixed in 14.0.6, which disables the legacy Liberty ID-FF endpoints.

t: Convene Azeus Convene Board Management Portal dummy_launcher.jsp cross site scripting
d: A vulnerability was determined in Convene Azeus Convene Board Management Portal 7.0.2.7_3 p72. The impacted element is an unknown function of the file /jsp/ge/dummy_launcher.jsp. Executing a manipulation of the argument REDIRECT_URL can lead to cross site scripting. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.
